intentions.title: Give developers a zero-to-running Barkpark app in one CLI command (create-barkpark-app)
intentions.evidence: index.ts orchestrates the full flow: prompts → scaffold → optional hosted-demo wiring → install → git init → printed next steps, mirroring create-next-app/create-vite UX; constants.ts exposes AVAILABLE_TEMPLATES=['website-starter','blog-starter'].

intentions.title: Let a prospect try Barkpark instantly against a public read-only hosted demo dataset, with a clear path to switch to local docker-compose later
intentions.evidence: hosted.ts applyHostedDemo() strips docker-compose files, writes .env.local pointing BARKPARK_API_URL at HOSTED_DEMO_URL (https://barkpark.dev), and flips on a HostedDemoBanner marker in app/layout.tsx; post-install.ts prints 'You are on the public hosted demo dataset (read-only)' plus instructions to re-run without --hosted-demo for local data.

intentions.title: Never leave a half-scaffolded or corrupted project directory behind, even on partial failure or bad input
intentions.evidence: index.ts ensureTargetEmpty() refuses to scaffold into a non-empty directory before any writes happen; scaffold.ts assertTemplateExists() fails fast with a named error; prompts.ts projectNameError() validates non-interactive names (rejecting empty/dot-leading) specifically because skipping that check previously let '.' or '/' normalize to cwd and produce a confusing downstream 'directory not empty' error instead of a clear message.

intentions.title: Support both fully interactive (clack prompts) and fully scripted/CI (--yes, flags) invocation without divergent validation paths
intentions.evidence: prompts.ts runPrompts() branches on yesFlag to short-circuit to defaults, but still runs projectNameError() on any inputs.targetArg before that branch so CLI-arg and --yes paths get the same validation as the interactive p.text validator; index.ts wires -t/--template, -y/--yes, --skip-install, --skip-git, --hosted-demo flags via commander.

intentions.title: Keep the scaffolder package-manager agnostic and safe to run offline/without installing
intentions.evidence: pm.ts detects the invoking package manager; install.ts wraps the actual install as a separate, catchable step so a failed install doesn't abort the whole scaffold (index.ts catches and prints a manual-install fallback); index.ts also supports --skip-install and --skip-git.

intentions.title: Render project templates safely with simple, auditable string substitution rather than a templating engine, and normalize arbitrary project names into valid npm package names
intentions.evidence: scaffold.ts renderTemplate() does a minimal {{key}} regex substitution over vars (projectName, packageName, pmCommand, barkparkVersion) applied only to recognized text-file extensions (isTextFile) or .tmpl files, binary files are fs.copyFile'd untouched; toPackageName() lowercases/strips/collapses into a valid slug, falling back to 'barkpark-site' if empty.
